transcript:
Header: Date/Time: 2026-09-11 14:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Raj (Citadel Edge - Head of ML), Sofia (Infra), Tom (Product)

Summary: quick discovery focused on unit economics. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference. Main ask: understand per-token pricing, how batching and prefix/KV caching change unit cost, and an estimated committed budget to meet 99th pct latency SLOs.

Topics: per-token vs reserved capacity, batching/caching levers, quantization effects on cost, security requirements (KMS, SSO), timeline for POC.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
00:12 Raj (Citadel Edge): yeah hi i'm raj head of ml. we've got sofia infra and tom product. thanks for doing this.
00:20 Liam (Redwood SE): hey all, liam here, i'll be digging into perf/cost tradeoffs.
00:30 Maya: great, agenda: walk current stack, traffic estimates, goals and budget, then we'll go into pricing options and batching/caching levers. sound good?
00:43 Raj: yep. high level first: we're a growth-stage startup doing realtime agent summarization and docs Q&A. typical prompt lengths are 100-300 tokens, often with a 1-2k doc context pulled in. cost is a big constraint - we have a monthly inference budget of about $50k for this team to start.
01:05 Tom: and latency target is <300ms p95 for the user-facing calls, with some background jobs ok at higher latency.
01:13 Sofia: security is a hard req; need KMS integration and audit logs, SSO.
01:20 Maya: good. quick Q to ground numbers: what are you seeing in qps today and expected ramp?
01:28 Raj: today low 10 RPS peak, expect to grow to 50-70 rps in 3 months, maybe 200-300 rps at scale. monthly token volume rough guess 4B tokens if growth hits the higher end.
01:45 Liam: ok that's helpful. so three modes to consider: hosted API (pay per-token), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), Private (VPC or on-prem). Each has different unit economics.
01:58 Maya: i'll run through pricing quickly — note these are illustrative and we'll send a spreadsheet. hosted is per-token with tiered discounts at volume, dedicated is committed capacity + lower per-token or flat instance pricing, private adds infra premium and setup.
02:15 Raj: can you quantify for our numbers? like with 4B tokens how different are we talking?
02:22 Maya: rough ballpark — hosted at our list might be $0.0006 per token for generation tier at that volume (we'll confirm), which would be about $2.4M — obviously that's outsized relative to your budget so we focus on caching, batching, and quantization to reduce effective tokens and cost.
02:45 Tom: whoa that's huge — so main question: what levers realistically get us into $50k-$100k range?
02:51 Liam: there are a few levers: 1) prefix/KV caching to avoid re-sending doc tokens on repeated queries, 2) aggressive batching to increase throughput per GPU (but can add latency), 3) model quantization / smaller model families for cheaper per-token compute, 4) dedicated/reserved capacity which drops compute cost per token.
03:12 Sofia: can you explain the caching part — we have docs that are referenced many times, do we re-send doc each call?
03:20 Liam: ideally no. with KV caching you store the doc embeddings and key-value states so repeat prompts referencing same doc only send the delta prompt. in practice we can cut token bill by 40-80% depending on reuse pattern. so if 4B tokens includes lots of repeated context, effective billable tokens might be 1.2B or lower.
03:47 Raj: that helps. any numbers on batching? we care about 300ms p95 so can't batch for too long.
03:55 Liam: batching is about grouping concurrent requests into a single GPU batch. at 50-70 rps we can use small, fast batching windows (10-30ms) to improve throughput with negligible added latency, reducing per-token compute cost by up to 20-30% relative to completely single-call serving. at 200 rps batching yields bigger wins. but p95 constraints limit batch wait times.
04:23 Maya: so combining caching + batching + smaller model variants is how customers often go from huge list-costs down into budget. we also offer reserved dedicated pools — you pay a monthly committed amount and get predictable throughput and lower effective cost per token.
04:39 Tom: what's the difference between dedicated and private?
04:42 Liam: dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware reserved for you, within our infra. private is VPC or on-prem where control plane is customer-side and there's network separation and extra compliance. private adds ops/setup and infra premiums.
04:58 Raj: given our budget - $50k initial - is it sensible to start hosted and then move to dedicated?
05:06 Maya: that's a common pattern. start hosted for quick launch, instrument tokens and caching, then once you have predictable traffic and need lower unit costs, shift to dedicated with a committed contract. we can model break-even points in the spreadsheet.
05:18 Sofia: about quantization — how much quality loss vs cost saving? we've got some hallucination sensitivity for docs Q&A.
05:26 Liam: quantization (8-bit or 4-bit) can reduce GPU memory and cost, with small quality regression for many tasks. for docs QA we usually recommend conservative quantization and run evals on your prompt set in the POC. we'll include recommended model variants and eval plan.
05:44 Raj: ok let's talk examples — suppose 4B tokens raw, but 60% of those are repeated doc context and can be cached, so billable tokens 1.6B; batching reduces compute cost 25% and dedicated reduces price per token further. what's rough cost?
06:01 Maya: if billable is 1.6B and effective per-token after batching/dedicated is $0.00015 then cost ~ $240k; still above target. to hit $50k you'd need more cache-hit ratio, smaller models for many calls, or stricter sampling/tempering to reduce token generation. also look at routing: send low-criticality calls to cheaper model variants.
06:27 Tom: what about hybrid — user-facing short prompts on dedicated low-latency models and long-doc background jobs onto cheaper private instances?
06:34 Liam: exactly. tiered routing reduces high-cost tokens. Redwood's smart routing can send by latency and cost policy, fallback to cheaper models during peaks.
06:45 Raj: security — we need KMS + SOC2 logs + SSO. do hosted options support that?
06:52 Maya: hosted supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs for enterprise tier; SSO + RBAC included. private gives you full network control. we'll include the security pack.
07:00 Sofia: any minimum commit for dedicated?
07:03 Maya: typical committed monthly is N GPUs for 6-12 months, but flexible options exist; we'll model a few sizing options in the spreadsheet.
07:12 Raj: timeline — we want to launch an MVP in 6 weeks, POC before then. is that realistic?
07:18 Liam: yes, start hosted now, instrument prompts and caching, run perf baseline and iterate. we can have an initial perf POC in 1-2 weeks.
07:28 Maya: ok we'll do that.

08:00 (Transcript continues with more detailed Q&A - timestamps every ~45s)
08:00 Liam: walk-through of a sample inference path: client -> API -> prefix cache check -> route to dedicated pool -> batch -> GPU call -> return. if cache hits earlier, we skip full context send.
08:20 Sofia: how do you measure cache hit ratios and evict policy?
08:25 Liam: metrics built-in: hit-rate, average saved tokens, evictions. policies can be LRU or TTL based and tuned per docs.
08:40 Raj: one worry: our documents are frequently updated, cache staleness. can we invalidate per doc id?
08:46 Liam: yes, cache keys tied to doc version id; you can explicitly invalidate on upload.
09:05 Tom: pricing question — are embeddings billed separately? we precompute for search, so are those separate line items?
09:12 Maya: yes embeddings are billed separately; if you do precompute locally you can cut embedding costs. we'll show that in the sheet.
09:30 Raj: any examples of customers that moved from hosted to dedicated and the delta?
09:34 Maya: yes — a fintech customer went from $300k/mo hosted to ~$80k/mo on dedicated after heavy caching and reserved capacity — different workloads vary though.
09:48 Sofia: SLA/uptime for dedicated?
09:50 Maya: SLA depends on contract tier, generally 99.9% or higher for dedicated. private can be supported to stricter controls.
10:05 Liam: on perf numbers, we'll run a short benchmark using your prompt set to produce p50/p95 latency by model variant and batching config.
10:20 Raj: good — what do you need from us for the benchmark?
10:24 Liam: sample prompt set (100-200 prompts), representative doc sizes, target latency SLOs, expected concurrency.
10:33 Raj: we'll email that by Monday.

12:00 (mid-call clarifications and small crosstalk; some words mangled)
12:05 Maya: quick note — when we say per-token cost, there are two parts: compute (GPU) and platform overhead. dedicated reduces compute; platform overhead can be reduced by caching/less calls.
12:22 Tom: ok real quick: given 50k budget, what's minimal approach?
12:27 Liam: short answer: start hosted, instrument caching aggressively, route high-volume low-sensitivity calls to smaller models; use dedupe and precompute where possible. if you hit sustained volume, move to small dedicated pool.
12:40 Raj: what about trial credits or pilot discounts?
12:44 Maya: we can offer trial credits and a short pilot discount for POC customers. details in follow-up.

18:00 (closing section)
18:05 Maya: recap of next steps: we'll send a pricing spreadsheet with three scenarios (hosted-only, hosted+dedicated ramp, private) and break-even models; Liam will run a perf baseline; Raj will send prompts.
18:20 Raj: thanks all, this was helpful.
18:25 Tom: thanks.
18:30 Maya: i'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf POC and the sizing call.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mislabels (speaker 2 sometimes appears as liam when question from tom), filler words, and minor mis-transcriptions like "Redbook" instead of Redwood.
